result.title: Beyond Random Starts: Amortized Initialization for Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Gradient-based transferable adversarial attacks achieve state-of-the-art attack success rates against black-box vision-language models (VLMs). However, they require hundreds of costly optimization steps for each image pair. One possible reason is that these attacks typically start from random perturbations that contain no information about the source or target image. In this work, we study whether amortized adversarial generation can provide better initializations for gradient-based attacks. By learning across many image pairs, amortization allows a generator to produce adversarial perturbations for new inputs without optimizing each perturbation from scratch. We introduce SPARK, a lightweight looped perturbation generator conditioned on both the source and target images. SPARK repeatedly applies the same network to refine a perturbation, producing effective adversarial attacks in a few forward passes without requiring gradients through surrogate vision encoders at inference time. We show that these perturbations provide effective warm starts for existing gradient-based attacks, substantially improving attack success rates while reducing the number of optimization steps required. These improvements generalize across different attack methods, VLMs, and unseen image categories. SPARK also produces effective standalone attacks at a fraction of the computational cost of gradient-based optimization. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/Patchwork53/SPARK.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPARK：一个以源图与目标图为条件的轻量循环扰动生成器，通过对多组图像对的摊销学习，用少量前向迭代反复细化扰动，为 VLM 黑盒对抗攻击提供热启动并降低梯度优化步数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享权重的循环网络少量迭代细化同一状态」和摊销初始化思路，可能为 LVR 的 looped latent 状态更新、初始状态设定与计算成本权衡提供线索，可供核查；但论文目标是攻击迁移而非视觉推理，未涉及 latent 语义内容是否被使用。
